title: Earthy Gooey Algerian Almond Butter Bao
description: A midnight-craving Algerian dish featuring almond butter and a unique nigiri-shaping technique that's low-glycemic-friendly. This recipe is perfect for a quick and satisfying dessert or snack.

ingredients.name: Active Dry Yeast
ingredients.notes: make sure to activate the yeast in warm almond milk before using

instructions: In a small bowl, combine warm almond milk and active dry yeast, let it sit for 5 minutes until the mixture becomes frothy.
In a large bowl, whisk together almond butter, granulated sugar, and unsalted butter until smooth.
Add the flour, baking soda, and salt to the wet ingredients and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and divide it into 4 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and then flatten it slightly into a disk shape.
Place a tablespoon of almond butter on one half of each disk, leaving a 1/2-inch border around the edges.
Fold the other half over the filling and press the edges together to seal the bao.
Place the baos on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving about 1 inch of space between each bao.
Bake the baos in the preheated oven for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown.
While the baos are baking, melt the dark chocolate chips in a double boiler or in the microwave in 30-second increments, stirring between each interval until smooth.
Once the baos are done, let them cool for 5 minutes before serving with melted dark chocolate drizzled on top.
To make the chocolate drizzle, simply place the melted chocolate in a piping bag or a zip-top plastic bag and snip off the corner to create a small hole.
Pipe the chocolate drizzle over the baos in a zig-zag pattern or your desired design.
